subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw add linux/riscv64 as an official Docker release platform now, and should that platform be non-blocking for existing amd64/arm64 releases?
rationale: This expands official release infrastructure and support expectations rather than fixing an already-defined broken release contract, so maintainer platform policy and validation requirements must be explicit before implementation.

options.title: Add non-blocking riscv64 images
options.body: Build riscv64 through QEMU, publish its digest only when successful, and require live release-path proof before treating it as official.

options.title: Defer official riscv64 Docker support
options.body: Leave the request open or close by explicit maintainer decision until dependency, Codex runtime, and release-capacity concerns are resolved.

options.title: Use an experimental separate image path
options.body: Publish riscv64 outside the main multi-arch manifest until reliability and support expectations are clear.

recommendation.title: Add non-blocking riscv64 images
recommendation.body: Build riscv64 through QEMU, publish its digest only when successful, and require live release-path proof before treating it as official.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release, Docker Hub, release-hardening, and Dockerfile history makes this the best available routing owner for the platform and ops decision.
